translation_en: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ubayd, from Salamah, who said: We pledged allegiance to the Prophet beneath the tree. He said to me, “Salamah, will you not pledge allegiance?” I said, “Messenger of Allah, I pledged allegiance the first time.” He said, “And do so the second time.”

Abdullah ibn Maslamah narrated to us, from Malik, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with them both: A Bedouin pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah upon Islam, then he was struck by fever. He said, “Release me from my pledge.” The Prophet refused. The man came again and said, “Release me from my pledge,” but he refused. The man then left. The Messenger of Allah said: “Madinah is like a furnace: it removes its impurities and its good becomes pure.”

Ali ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Abdullah ibn Yazid narrated to us; Said (meaning Ibn Abi Ayyub) narrated to us, who said: Abu Aqil, Zuhrah ibn Mabid, narrated to me, from his grandfather Abdullah ibn Hisham, who had met the Prophet. His mother, Zaynab daughter of Humayd, took him to the Messenger of Allah and said, “Messenger of Allah, accept his pledge.” The Prophet said: “He is still a child.” He wiped his head and prayed for him. He used to offer one sheep as a sacrifice on behalf of all his family.

Abdullah ibn Yusuf narrated to us; Malik informed us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn Abdullah: A Bedouin pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah upon Islam, then fever struck him in Madinah. He came to the Messenger of Allah and said, “Messenger of Allah, release me from my pledge.” The Messenger of Allah refused. He came again and said, “Release me from my pledge,” and he refused. He came a third time and said, “Release me from my pledge,” and he refused. The Bedouin then left. The Messenger of Allah said: “Madinah is like a furnace: it removes its impurities and its good becomes pure.”

Abdan narrated to us, from Abu Hamzah, from al-Amash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: “There are three to whom Allah will not speak on the Day of Resurrection, nor purify them, and for whom there will be a painful punishment: a man who has surplus water on a road and withholds it from a traveler; a man who pledges allegiance to a leader only for worldly gain, so that if he gives him what he wants he keeps faith with him, but if not, he does not; and a man who makes a sale to another after the afternoon prayer, swears by Allah that he was offered such-and-such for it, and the buyer believes him and takes it, although he was not offered that amount.”

Abu al-Yaman narrated to us; Shuaib informed us, from al-Zuhri. Al-Layth said: Yunus narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, who informed me that Abu Idris al-Khawlani heard Ubadah ibn al-Samit say: The Messenger of Allah said to us while we were gathered: “Will you pledge to me that you will not associate anything with Allah, steal, commit adultery, kill your children, bring a false accusation that you fabricate between your hands and legs, or disobey in what is right? Whoever among you fulfills this, his reward is with Allah. Whoever commits any of these acts and is punished for it in this world, that punishment is an expiation for him. Whoever commits any of them and Allah conceals it, then his case rests with Allah: if He wills, He will punish him, and if He wills, He will forgive him.” So we pledged to him on that basis.

Mahmud narrated to us; Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us; Mamar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah, from Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Prophet used to accept women’s pledges verbally, in accordance with this verse: “that they will not associate anything with Allah” (60:12). Aishah said: The Messenger of Allah’s hand never touched a woman’s hand, except a woman whom he owned.

Musaddad narrated to us; Abd al-Warith narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Hafsah, from Umm Atiyyah, who said: We pledged allegiance to the Prophet, and he recited to me: “that they will not associate anything with Allah” (60:12). He forbade us to lament the dead. One woman among us withdrew her hand and said, “So-and-so comforted me, and I want to repay her.” He said nothing. She later returned. None of the women fulfilled the pledge except Umm Sulaym, Umm al-Ala, and the daughter of Abu Sabrah, the wife of Muadh—or the daughter of Abu Sabrah and the wife of Muadh.

Abu Nuaym narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, who said: I heard Jabir say: A Bedouin came to the Prophet and said, “Accept my pledge to Islam.” He accepted his pledge. The next day the man came with a fever and said, “Release me from it.” The Prophet refused. When the man turned away, he said: “Madinah is like a furnace: it removes its impurities and its good becomes pure.”

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us; Sulayman ibn Bilal informed us, from Yahya ibn Said, who said: I heard al-Qasim ibn Muhammad say that Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said, “Oh, my head!” The Messenger of Allah said: “That would be no problem if it happened while I was alive; I would ask Allah to forgive you and pray for you.” Aishah said, “What a loss! By Allah, I think you want me to die. If that happened, you would spend the rest of that day with one of your wives.” The Prophet said: “No, it is I who say, ‘Oh, my head!’ I had intended—or wanted—to send for Abu Bakr and his son and make a stipulation, lest someone make claims or wish for things.” Then I said, “Allah will not allow it, and the believers will prevent it,” or, “Allah will prevent it, and the believers will not allow it.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us; Sufyan informed us, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: Umar was asked, “Will you appoint a successor?” He said: “If I appoint one, someone better than me, Abu Bakr, appointed a successor. If I leave it, someone better than me, the Messenger of Allah, left it.” They praised him, and he said: “I am neither eager for it nor seeking to escape it. I wish I could be free of it with neither gain nor blame, and not have to bear it alive or dead.”

Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us; Hisham informed us, from Mamar, from al-Zuhri. Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, informed me that he heard Umar’s final sermon when Umar sat on the pulpit, the day after the Prophet died. Umar testified, while Abu Bakr remained silent and did not speak: “I had hoped that the Messenger of Allah would live until he was the last of us to die. If Muhammad has died, Allah has left among you a light by which you are guided, through what Allah guided Muhammad. Abu Bakr is the Companion of the Messenger of Allah, the second of the two, and the most entitled among the Muslims to manage your affairs. So stand and pledge allegiance to him.” Some people had already pledged to him at the portico of Banu Saidah; the public pledge was on the pulpit. Al-Zuhri reported from Anas ibn Malik that Umar said to Abu Bakr that day, “Ascend the pulpit.” Umar kept urging him until he ascended it, and the people at large pledged allegiance to him.

Abd al-Aziz ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Ibrahim ibn Sad narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mutim, from his father, who said: A woman came to the Prophet and spoke to him about something. He told her to return to him. She said, “Messenger of Allah, what if I come and do not find you?”—as if she meant his death. He said: “If you do not find me, then go to Abu Bakr.”

Musaddad narrated to us; Yahya narrated to us, from Sufyan; Qays ibn Muslim narrated to me, from Tariq ibn Shihab, from Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said to the delegation of Buzakhah: “You will follow the camels’ trails until Allah shows the successor of His Prophet and the Emigrants a course of action toward you for which they may excuse you.”

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me; Ghundar narrated to us; Shubah narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik, who said: I heard Jabir ibn Samurah say: I heard the Prophet say: “There will be twelve commanders.” He said a word I did not hear. My father said he said: “All of them will be from Quraysh.”

Ismail narrated to us; Malik narrated to me, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-Araj, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I considered ordering firewood to be gathered, then ordering the prayer and having the call made for it, then appointing a man to lead the people in prayer, and then going to men who stay behind and burning their houses over them. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if one of them knew that he would find a meaty bone or two good pieces of meat, he would attend the evening prayer.” Muhammad ibn Yusuf said: Yunus said: Muhammad ibn Sulayman said: Abu Abdullah explained that a mirmah is a piece of meat between the sheep’s hoof, like a small stick; the meem is vowelled with kasrah.

Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to me; al-Layth narrated to us, from Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abdullah ibn Kab ibn Malik, that Abdullah ibn Kab ibn Malik—who used to guide his father Kab, who had become blind—said: I heard Kab ibn Malik say: When he stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah during the expedition to Tabuk, he related his account. The Messenger of Allah forbade the Muslims to speak to us, and we remained in that state for fifty nights. Then the Messenger of Allah announced that Allah had accepted our repentance.

Said ibn Ufayr narrated to us; al-Layth narrated to me; Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Salamah and Said ibn al-Musayyab, that Abu Hurayrah said: I heard the Messenger of Allah say: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, were it not that some men dislike being left behind after me, and that I have no mounts to carry them, I would not remain behind from any expedition. I would love to be killed in the path of Allah, then brought back to life, then killed, then brought back to life, then killed.”

Abdullah ibn Yusuf narrated to us; Malik informed us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-Araj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I would love to fight in the path of Allah and be killed, then be brought back to life, then be killed, then brought back to life, then be killed, then be brought back to life.” Abu Hurayrah used to say these words three times, affirming: “I swear by Allah.”

Ishaq ibn Nasr narrated to us; Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, from Mamar, from Hammam, who heard Abu Hurayrah narrate from the Prophet, who said: “If I had gold equal to Mount Uhud, I would love for three nights not to pass while I still had any of it with me, except something I set aside to repay a debt, if I could find someone to accept it.”

Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us; al-Layth narrated to us, from Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Urwah told me that Aishah said: The Messenger of Allah said: “If I had known beforehand what I later came to know, I would not have brought the sacrificial animals, and I would have left the consecrated state along with the people when they did.”

Al-Hasan ibn Umar narrated to us; Yazid narrated to us, from Habib, from Ata, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: We set out with the Messenger of Allah proclaiming the pilgrimage, and we arrived in Mecca on the fourth day of Dhu al-Hijjah. The Prophet ordered us to circumambulate the House and Safa and Marwah, make it an umrah, and leave the consecrated state, except those who had brought sacrificial animals. None of us had brought an animal except the Prophet and Talhah. Ali came from Yemen with sacrificial animals and said, “I entered consecration for what the Messenger of Allah entered consecration for.” They said, “Shall we go to Mina while one of us is still dripping?” The Messenger of Allah said: “If I had known beforehand what I later came to know, I would not have brought a sacrificial animal; and were it not that I have one with me, I would leave the consecrated state.” Suraqah met him while he was stoning Jamrat al-Aqabah and asked, “Messenger of Allah, is this concession only for us?” He said: “No, it is for all time.” Aishah had arrived in Mecca menstruating. The Prophet ordered her to perform all the rites except circumambulation and prayer until she became pure. When they stopped at al-Batha, Aishah said, “Messenger of Allah, you are going with a pilgrimage and an umrah, while I am going with only a pilgrimage.” He then ordered Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr to go with her to al-Tanim, and she performed an umrah in Dhu al-Hijjah after the days of pilgrimage.

Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to us; Sulayman ibn Bilal narrated to us; Yahya ibn Said narrated to me, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Amir ibn Rabiah say that Aishah said: One night the Prophet could not sleep and said: “Would that a righteous man among my Companions would guard me tonight.” Then we heard the sound of weapons. He said, “Who is that?” It was said, “It is Sad, Messenger of Allah. I have come to guard you.” The Prophet slept until we heard his breathing. Abu Abdullah said: Aishah reported that Bilal said: “Would that I knew whether I would spend a night in a valley, with idhkhir and jalil around me.” I told the Prophet about it.

Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us; Jarir narrated to us, from al-Amash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: “There is no envy except in two cases: a man whom Allah has given the Quran, who recites it during the hours of the night and day and says, ‘If I had been given what this man has been given, I would do as he does’; and a man whom Allah has given wealth and who spends it rightly, saying, ‘If I had been given what this man has been given, I would do as he does.’” Qutaybah narrated to us; Jarir narrated to us with the same wording.

Hasan ibn al-Rabi narrated to us; Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Asim, from al-Nadr ibn Anas, who said: Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: If I had not heard the Prophet say, “Do not wish for death,” I would have wished for it.

Muhammad narrated to us; Abdah narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Khalid, from Qays, who said: We went to visit Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, who had been cauterized seven times. He said: “Were it not that the Messenger of Allah forbade us to pray for death, I would have prayed for it.”

Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us; Hisham ibn Yusuf narrated to us; Mamar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Ubayd—whose name was Sad ibn Ubayd, the freedman of Abd al-Rahman ibn Azhar—from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said: “None of you should wish for death. If he is doing good, perhaps he will increase in good; and if he is doing wrong, perhaps he will seek to make amends.”

Abdan narrated to us; my father informed me, from Shubah. Abu Ishaq narrated to us, from al-Bara ibn Azib, who said: On the day of the Confederates, the Prophet carried earth with us. I saw the dust cover the whiteness of his stomach as he said: “Were it not for You, we would not have been guided, nor given charity, nor prayed. Send tranquility down upon us. The people have rebelled against us; when they intend a trial, we refuse.” He raised his voice with the words “we refuse.”

Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to me; Muawiyah ibn Amr narrated to us; Abu Ishaq narrated to us, from Musa ibn Uqbah, from Salim Abu al-Nadr, the freedman of Umar ibn Ubaydullah, who was his scribe. He said: Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa wrote to him, and I read the letter. It said that the Messenger of Allah said: “Do not wish to meet the enemy; ask Allah for well-being.”

Ali ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us; Abu al-Zinad narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, who said: Ibn Abbas mentioned the two spouses who invoked mutual curses. Abdullah ibn Shaddad said, “Is she the woman about whom the Messenger of Allah said, ‘If I were to stone a woman without clear proof’?” He replied, “No. That was a woman who had openly committed adultery.”
